title: Add RAG mosaic authoring stubs and live-preview quickstart
author: Lena Morales
release_notes: Introduce a compact quickstart that demonstrates a 'mosaic' authoring pattern for RAG scenarios: template stubs, a live preview server, telemetry probes, and a devcontainer for local onboarding.
description:
Motivation and summary: Add a lightweight quickstart that shows authors how to compose retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios using a 'mosaic' layout: small, composable step templates (retrieval, transform, tool-call, finalization) that can be arranged and previewed in real time. This is targeted at developer-first product teams who want fast iteration cycles when authoring multi-step agents and tool-calling flows. The quickstart includes: 1) starter templates for step types, 2) a tiny live-preview server that streams intermediate step outputs into a mosaic UI, 3) telemetry probes and example probes for Redwood Console, 4) a devcontainer and scripts to run locally, and 5) CI e2e smoke tests.

What changed (high-level): commits: - Add mosaic authoring templates and README (initial scaffolding) - Add live-preview server (FastAPI + SSE) and browser UI - Wire telemetry probe hooks and example telemetry config - Add devcontainer, Makefile and local-run scripts - Add CI smoke test that runs quickstart e2e in headless mode - Docs site section and short how-to guide

Changed areas/files (representative): - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/README.md (new authoring guide and examples) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/templates/*.yaml (retrieval/transform/tool/output stubs) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/live-preview/server.py (SSE endpoints + example runner) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/live-preview/static/index.html (mosaic UI) - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/devcontainer.json + .devcontainer/Dockerfile - quickstarts/rag-mosaic/telemetry/probes.yaml - .github/workflows/quickstart-e2e.yml (added smoke job) - docs/site/content/quickstarts/rag-mosaic.md (documentation and screenshots)

Usage and run instructions (short): 1) git checkout feature/rag-mosaic-authoring-live-preview 2) cd quickstarts/rag-mosaic 3) ./dev.sh start (boots local index, preview server, and sample index) 4) Open http://localhost:8080 to interact with mosaic editor and live preview The quickstart ships with a small seeded index (sqlite + json files) and an in-memory mock tool for safe local iteration.

Design notes and rationale: - Mosaic layout: each step emits a compact envelope {type, summary, tokens_used, result_preview}. The UI displays envelopes tiled so authors can quickly inspect how retrieval, rerank, transform, and tool calls interact. - Live preview uses SSE to avoid full-page polling; server-side runner replays a seeded conversation and emits step-level deltas to the UI. This mirrors production tracing while remaining lightweight for local runs. - Telemetry probes: small hooks are emitted from the runner with route and token-level metadata; default probes are no-op but wired to Redwood Console examples in telemetry/probes.yaml. - Templates: YAML-based step templates were chosen for readability and copy/paste ergonomics in docs and repos. Templates include sensible defaults for caching/batching hints and an example quantization/throughput note.

Testing and CI: - Added a headless CI job quickstart-e2e that launches the preview server, runs a scripted interaction via curl/WebSocket, and validates expected envelopes are emitted. - Initial runs flagged a flaky timing issue in the SSE client; fixed by adding a small backoff and a readiness probe in server.py. Current CI: pass (2026-02-12) — run summary: lint: pass, unit: pass, smoke-e2e: pass after 1 rerun.

Review conversation (highlights): - Chris Nguyen: "Nice UX—can we make the templates explicit about token budget guidance?" => Author: "Added 'token_budget' field and inline guidance in templates/README." - Maya Patel: "Telemetry probes look sensible; only ask is to keep them opt-in by default." => Author: "Probes are opt-in; default probes.yaml is commented with usage and a small snippet to hook to Redwood Console." - Jonah Reyes: "CI smoke job duplicated some logic from other quickstarts, consider extracting helpers." => Author: "Pulled common e2e helpers into .github/actions/quickstart-utils and updated workflow." - Maya: "Approve after CI green." - Chris: "Approve." Merge: squash-and-merge by Lena Morales on 2026-02-12.

Backwards compatibility and risks: - No breaking changes to existing APIs or docs. The quickstart is additive and isolated under quickstarts/rag-mosaic. - Risk: SSE behavior might differ across browsers; added guidance in README with fallback polling option and a small compatibility test in the e2e job.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - ENG-1987: Add a small workshop notebook that uses the mosaic quickstart for hands-on developer sessions. - DES-145: Iterate on UI affordances (drag-to-reorder, inline assertions). - PM-222: Measure authoring iteration time in the wild (opt-in telemetry).

Related items and links: - Linear: ENG-1987, PM-222, DES-145 - Internal doc: docs/site/content/quickstarts/rag-mosaic.md - Example demo build (assets): quickstarts/rag-mosaic/live-preview/fixtures/demo.json

Notes: kept the description intentionally compact and focused on developer onboarding, low-friction iteration, and telemetry safety. The quickstart intentionally avoids production-grade index setup and instead demonstrates wiring and UX patterns for teams to adapt to their infra.
